newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wholesale prices up first time in 13 months.
newsitem.headline: German wholesale prices up first time in 13 months.

text.p: German wholesale prices, fuelled by a jump in oil prices, posted their first year-on-year rise in 13 months in October, data released by the Federal Statistics Office on Monday showed.
Wholesale prices rose by 0.9 percent against the same month a year earlier, after falling by 0.7 percent in September.

Compared to the previous month, prices were up by 0.2 percent after a 0.1 percent fall in September. In October 1995, prices had fallen by a monthly 1.4 percent -- ushering in a run of wholesale price deflation which has now been broken.
Key components of the wholesale price index driving the rise were heating oil, up 13 percent and diesel fuel, up 6.8 percent. Motor gasoline, however, was up just 0.9 percent.
